data.description:
## Observation
A full `make verify` on macOS/arm64 (worktree fix-bd66-detector-flake, origin/main b4e0d01b649 plus a test-only change to tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`, 2026-11-16, host load average 40-70 on 18 CPUs with other sessions' verifies running) ended `4 failed, 21291 passed, 29 skipped in 10796.46s (2:59:56)`:

- tests/scripts/test_observability_reviewbot_webhook_auth.py::test_reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections_publish_from_health_payload
- tests/scripts/test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py::test_shrinking_journal_publishes_zero_not_the_remaining_total[replication_errors-REPL_OFFSET_FILE]
- tests/scripts/test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py::test_shrinking_journal_publishes_zero_not_the_remaining_total[voter_errors-VOTER_OFFSET_FILE]
- tests/scripts/test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py::test_markers_after_a_rotation_still_publish

All 4 raised `subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['bash', '.../infra/scripts/observability.sh']' timed out after 60 seconds` from `run_observability(..., timeout=60)`. The same 2 files run alone right after: `10 passed in 89.99s`.

## What is not established
Why one stubbed observability.sh run takes over 60 s under load (the stubs replace curl/aws/journalctl). Candidates to distinguish: per-run process count of the script (many short subprocesses, each slowed by load), a stub that blocks, or lock/sleep waits inside the script.

## Approach
Reproduce deterministically (scale the 60 s bound down, or measure the script's subprocess count and wall time per run), identify the cost driver, and fix the class: bound what the test asks the script to do rather than raising the wall-clock bound. No production behaviour change unless the cost is in the script itself.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The cost driver of a stubbed observability.sh run is measured and recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] The 4 tests pass with the cause fixed at class level, without raising the 60 s bound and without retries.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
data.title: Flaky: observability.sh tests time out at their 60 s subprocess bound under full-suite load
